entry.title: Walk India's heritage
entry.line: Every stone here remembers a story.
overview.clickToGo: Click the wheel to go there
reel.1: Long ago, on the eastern coast of India, in the land we now call Odisha, fishermen pushed their boats out before dawn. Every morning, they watched the sun rise, red and gold, out of the sea. And they told a story about it.
reel.2: The sun, they said, is Surya, a god who rides across the sky in a golden chariot. Seven white horses pull it through the clouds, one for each day of the week. Its great wheels turn the hours, the months, and the seasons of the year.
reel.3: Around the year 1250, a king of Odisha, Narasimha Deva the First, stood on this shore. He had won great wars, and he wished to thank the Sun. So he chose to do something bold. He would build Surya's chariot on earth, in stone, here, beside the sea.
reel.4: Tradition says that twelve hundred artisans worked for twelve years. Stone came by river, and elephants hauled it into place. Block by block, the temple rose, and the carvers covered every wall with life: dancers and musicians, hunters and lovers, elephants, horses, and kings.
reel.5: Along its base, they carved twenty-four great wheels, each one taller than a man. Every wheel has eight wide spokes and eight slender ones, and every inch is carved. Some say that, even now, the shadow of a spoke can tell you the time of day.
reel.6: Nearly eight centuries have passed. The great tower has fallen, and the sea has moved away. But the audience hall still stands, facing the morning sun, just as its makers intended. This is Konark, the chariot of the Sun. Come, let us walk inside it.
reel.title: Konark
